diagnosis.root_cause: Two active CRM records, lineids 4C:D7:C8:93:BA:F1 and 4C:D7:C8:7F:0A:B9, are assigned to the same physical ONU slot EPON0/4:17. Only one ONU can occupy that slot, creating a provisioning and identity conflict.
evidence: The live ONU is responding and online, with Auth/Finish state, normal RX power of -20.91 dBm, normal TX power of 2.38 dBm, and normal VLAN 1044.
The seven-day optical telemetry is stable: RX remains around -21 dBm, TX around +2.3 dBm, distance is constant at 134, and TX bias remains within the healthy 9.5-13.0 mA range.
The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, all eight PONs are healthy, and OLT CPU, memory, and temperature are normal; this rules out an OLT, PON, splitter, or router fault.
Peers on EPON0/4 are online with healthy optical readings, ruling out a shared physical fault.

The subscriber has only two sessions in 24 hours with an average duration near the network mean, and RADIUS data is present and CRM-consistent, ruling out session flapping and the listed RADIUS faults.
The duplicate_onu_slot record explicitly shows two different active ONU line IDs assigned to EPON0/4:17, which is the direct fault evidence.

remediation.action: Verify the physical ONU MAC currently present on EPON0/4:17, then correct the CRM/OLT inventory so the real ONU has the slot and the stale or incorrect record is removed or moved to its proper slot. Reconcile the associated RADIUS and line-ID mappings afterward, and rescan the port to confirm unique ONU assignments.

ground_truth.root_cause: Two active CRM records place different ONU MACs on EPON0/4:17. A slot holds exactly one ONU, so one record is stale. The live probe returns a single device, and its MAC matches the subject record, identifying the other as the leftover.
expected_reasoning: The CRM view lists two active customers on EPON0/4:17 with different ONU MACs
A PON slot holds exactly one ONU, so this state is physically impossible
The live probe of that slot returns a single responding device
The probe's optical values match the subject record's cached reading of -20.88 dBm
RADIUS holds a consistent entry for the subject with normal sessions and traffic
The second record therefore does not correspond to an installed device and is stale
The optical layer is healthy and neither customer is experiencing a service fault
This is a record defect of the same class as the 644 such interfaces in the estate

expected_escalation.review_reason: One of two CRM records on this slot is stale; deleting the wrong one disconnects a live customer

distractors: Nothing is failing and no customer has complained
Both records are marked active and look equally legitimate in CRM
